# Caddy config for the substrate VM: the single public listener fronting every surface, routed by
# hostname.
#
# cycsail.team (SITE_DOMAIN): every request is gated by oauth2-proxy (Google), restricted to
# members of the all@ group, so reaching the static files at all IS the authorization check — the
# portal itself is a purely static site with no backend.
#
# directus.* (DIRECTUS_DOMAIN): the CRM's data layer (Directus itself — an admin screen, not
# customer-facing). No oauth2-proxy gate here — Directus authenticates via its own native Google
# OIDC and enforces its own roles/permissions server-side, so this is a plain reverse proxy.
#
# Both domains are provided by the compose environment so the same image works for any domain.

{$DIRECTUS_DOMAIN} {
	reverse_proxy directus:8055
}

{$SITE_DOMAIN} {
	# oauth2-proxy's own endpoints (sign-in, callback, sign-out) must be reachable unauthenticated.
	handle /oauth2/* {
    "cat > /var/substrate/substrate.env <<EOF",
    `CADDY_IMAGE=${image}`,
    `SITE_DOMAIN=${siteDomain}`,
    `DIRECTUS_DOMAIN=${directusDomain}`,
    `OAUTH2_PROXY_GOOGLE_GROUP=${authGroup}`,
    `OAUTH2_PROXY_GOOGLE_ADMIN_EMAIL=${authAdminEmail}`,
    "GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=$(fetch_secret google-oauth-client-id)",
    "GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=$(fetch_secret google-oauth-client-secret)",
    // oauth2-proxy needs URL-safe base64; the stored secret may be standard base64 (same bytes).
    "OAUTH2_PROXY_COOKIE_SECRET=$(fetch_secret portal-oauth-cookie-secret | tr -- '+/' '-_')",
    `DIRECTUS_DB_HOST=${directusDbHost}`,
    `DIRECTUS_ADMIN_EMAIL=${directusAdminEmail}`,
    "DIRECTUS_KEY=$(fetch_secret directus-key)",
    "DIRECTUS_SECRET=$(fetch_secret directus-secret)",
    "DIRECTUS_DB_PASSWORD=REDACTED directus-db-password)",
    "DIRECTUS_ADMIN_PASSWORD=$(fetch_secret directus-admin-bootstrap-password)",
    // Optional: Directus runs on the Core tier if empty. See docs/manual-setup.md §6.
    "DIRECTUS_LICENSE_KEY=$(fetch_secret directus-license-key || true)",

content.text:
I rechecked Porkbun's own name servers directly, so this is the current state, not a cached copy.

| Record | Status |
| --- | --- |
| SPF | ✅ Fixed. One record: `v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com include:amazonses.com ~all` |
| SES MX at the root | ✅ Removed. Mail routes only to Google now. |
| Stray DMARC at the root | ✅ Removed. |
| DKIM | ❌ Not found |

For DKIM, I checked the default `google._domainkey` name, several common custom names, and the doubled name Porkbun creates when the host field includes the domain. None has a key.

A setting showing DKIM as enabled and an empty DNS lookup can both be true. The admin console generates the key before the DNS record exists, and "Start authentication" only works once Google can find that record. To see which situation you're in:

1. **Check the admin console.** Go to Apps → Google Workspace → Gmail → **Authenticate email** and pick `cyccommunitysailing.org`.
   - If it says **"Authenticating email with DKIM,"** DKIM is on, and the page shows the **DNS host name** it uses. Send me that name and I'll look it up; it may be one I didn't guess.
   - If it says **"Not authenticating,"** the key exists but isn't published. Copy the TXT value from that page into Porkbun with host `google._domainkey` (just that; Porkbun adds the domain), wait for it to show up, then click **Start authentication**.
2. **Check a real message.** Send a message from your Workspace account to any outside Gmail address. Open it there, then choose ⋮ → **Show original**. If DKIM is working, it shows `DKIM: 'PASS' with domain cyccommunitysailing.org`. If it names a `gappssmtp.com` domain instead, Google is using its fallback signature, which doesn't count toward DMARC.

Either check settles it. Once DKIM passes, the email fixes for step 4 are complete. Only the SMTP relay rule for the VM's IP will remain, and it isn't needed until Authentik starts sending codes.

On the build side, step 2 is done and committed as `28913d09`: it adds the three relation aliases the roster rules need. Build, lint, and all 504 tests pass. Step 5, adding Authentik's database, secrets, and containers, is next. I'm checking one thing before dispatching it: whether changing the VM's startup script replaces the VM. That would briefly take Directus and the portal offline, and if so I'll tell you before it deploys.

Google says Authenticating email with DKIM: DNS Host name (TXT record name):
dkim._domainkey
